players.product: Integrated data-center power + thermal + rack systems (CPI / SpinCo: grid-to-chip)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2026 results (CEO/CFO): 'Revenue came in at $7.1 billion, up 8% versus last year, and adjusted operating margin was 6.5%'; adjusted EPS was $0.87, up 13%, a record. CFO: revenue growth was 'driven by continued strong performance in data center and improving momentum in our Industrial and Health Solutions businesses'; adjusted gross profit $690 million at a 9.8% adjusted gross margin; adjusted operating profit $460 million, operating margin up 40 basis points year-over-year (a record), reflecting 'our deliberate shift towards higher value products and services'.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $7.1 billion (up 8%); adjusted operating margin 6.5% (up 40 basis points); adjusted EPS $0.87 (up 13%); adjusted gross margin 9.8%

quarterly_data.signal: The data center portfolio is 'built around three tightly connected capabilities: compute integration, cooling, and power.' Quarter milestones (CEO): 'We announced the development of modular data center systems with NVIDIA, reimagining deployment for speed and scale, as well as a partnership with LG to advance thermal management solutions designed for gigawatt-scale data centers. We also deployed our advanced rack-level vertically integrated liquid cooling at the Equinix co-innovation facility'. Flex also introduced 'the new AI infrastructure platform, the first globally manufactured data center platform to integrate power, cooling, compute, and services into a modular design', which can accelerate deployment timelines by up to 30%.
quarterly_data.figure: new AI infrastructure platform accelerates deployment timelines by up to 30%

quarterly_data.signal: Data center growth on track (CEO): 'data center growth remains on track for what we have said for the full-year guide', to be updated when the fiscal year closes. The 35% growth rate for data center assumed 'pretty decent growth with our hyperscale customer, and it is playing out the way we imagined it to be'; the customer consigned inventory mix shift affects some of these growth rates. Both power and compute 'are growing very, very strongly, whether it's embedded power or critical power or the compute side.'
quarterly_data.figure: 35% growth rate for data center (FY2026 guide, on track)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity investment plan (CEO): 'Power has been more heavy this year in terms of investments for capacity'. Because of 'the large AI infrastructure spend' and 'new programs coming on board for compute', Flex expects to invest more in compute capacity over the next few years. For next year: 'we'll be adding probably more capacity in our embedded power business. Not as much in our critical power business because we'll be digesting the capacity we're adding this year.' 'our biggest investments are still happening in North America', and 'most of our investments are being driven by what's expected in the US and in Mexico.' CFO: Q3 net CapEx was $145 million, or approximately 2% of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 net CapEx $145 million (approximately 2% of revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: Agility segment (CFO): revenue $3.8 billion, up 6% year-over-year. 'Data center-related end markets continue to drive strong growth but were partially offset by softness in our consumer-related end markets'; adjusted operating margin 6.3%, flat year-over-year. CEO: the extra Agility upside 'is driven by kind of what is happening in high-speed networking or network interface cards'. Flex does not count these in its data center business, but they are 'data center-related infrastructure deployments'. The prepared remarks also cite 'high-performance networking and satellite communication products' as AI-driven strength outside data center. Q4 guide: Agility up low to mid-single digits 'as cloud and networking growth is offset by softer demand for consumer devices and lifestyle.'
quarterly_data.figure: Agility revenue $3.8 billion (up 6%); adjusted operating margin 6.3%

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance raised (CFO): 'Revenue to be between $27.2 billion and $27.5 billion, which is $350 million higher at the midpoint versus our prior guide'; adjusted operating margin of approximately 6.3%; adjusted EPS between $3.21 and $3.27, a midpoint increase of $0.11; 80% plus free cash flow conversion maintained. The CFO also gave a total-Flex outlook of revenue between $6.75 billion and $7.05 billion, adjusted operating income of $445 million to $475 million, and adjusted EPS between $0.83 and $0.89 per share on approximately 375 million weighted average shares; the transcript introduces it as 'segment outlook for the year' but places it after the Slide 13 fourth-quarter guidance, so its period is not clearly stated.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue between $27.2 billion and $27.5 billion ($350 million higher at the midpoint); adjusted operating margin approximately 6.3%; adjusted EPS between $3.21 and $3.27

quarterly_data.signal: Memory price spike (CEO): apart from the memory Flex uses in its own power-side products, customers buy memory themselves ('procured by our customers directly from the memory suppliers'). Memory makers are 'selecting few end markets more than the others. So you are seeing a bigger distribution go to data centers'. Consumer demand shows no significant effect because those markets 'are soft to begin with', but 'there is allocation of material that is happening, and, you know, we bake that into our forecast.'

connects_to.relationship: hyperscale data-center customer (AWS program tied to the Amazon warrant)

contracts.signal: Asked whether the Amazon warrant deal is already adding upside, CFO: 'the warrants are not incremental, nor were they expected to be materially incremental to FY 2026. So it's really that program as we move forward is where we'd expect to see that. Deployments are complex, and they scale over time.' CEO: the 35% data center growth rate assumed 'pretty decent growth with our hyperscale customer, and it is playing out the way we imagined it to be', and 'our growth with AWS is very strong, and it's going as expected. And we continue to expect to see that growth rate continue into the next few years.'

players.product: merchant power supplies / power shelves (FlexPower) for AI racks

quarterly_data.signal: Embedded vs critical power (CEO): both 'are growing very, very strongly'. Critical power depends on lead times and installations, mostly 'putting these large power pods in', and there 'we compete with the traditional electrical players'. Embedded power 'is going through a huge technology shift with what is happening in the 800-volt DC category, larger one-megawatt deployments in terms of rack power itself'. 'We are at the forefront of that technology shift. There are only a very small group of competitors who play in that space.' Management expects embedded power growth 'to accelerate with these large power deployments', citing '800-volt DC and larger megawatt deployments that are happening across hyperscalers.'
quarterly_data.figure: 800-volt DC; larger one-megawatt rack power deployments

quarterly_data.signal: Reliability segment, driven by power (CFO): revenue accelerated to $3.2 billion, up 10%. 'Power continues to drive strong growth alongside core industrial and health solutions'. Adjusted operating income was $233 million; adjusted operating margin was 7.2%, up 50 basis points, 'driven by power and core industrial'. Asked what drove the sequential margin gain, the CFO said 'it was power, power mix, and core industrial'. Guide: Q4 Reliability revenue up low double digits to mid-teens, 'driven by continued strength in power'; full-year Reliability up mid-single digits, 'driven by strong data center power demand'.
quarterly_data.figure: Reliability revenue $3.2 billion (up 10%); adjusted operating margin 7.2% (up 50 basis points)

connects_to.relationship: power supplies (PSU/BBU/800V DC) for GPU racks
